title: Packs
summary: Diceroll's Releases page on the Packs tab: the four content packs declared in .pkey/release with type, delivery, latest version, gate and size; the supporter pack's manifest gate waiting for one approval on Access; and how packs reach players on each channel, picked automatically, with the CDN fallback said where a store transport can't be used yet.
compare: Packs are releases, so they sit under Releases (App and Packs tabs) in Diceroll's Product context, Release accent; no separate Packs nav item and no page subtitle (the tabs say it).

The pack table uses the manifest's names (diceroll.core3d, diceroll.supporter.skins, diceroll.foes, diceroll.l10n) and says type, delivery in words (Essential, the baseline shipping in each build; On demand; newest that fits contentApi 3–4; per language), latest version, gate (a dash when none) and size; its foot says they are declared in .pkey/release.

P4-34: a pack whose manifest asserts a gate shows it as 'To approve' with the flag name in the Gate column; a warning callout says what waits (CI can't publish diceroll.supporter.skins 1.4.0) and why (its manifest asks for the gate extras.diceSkins, which needs one approval), with 'Approve on Access'. The gate is never typed again here. 'Sold as the Dice skins add-on' links the pack to what sells it.

P4-33: 'How packs reach players' lists each channel as a row with its store mark and where packs come from, picked automatically: the App Store falls back to Polaris Key's CDN with a warning that says why (Background Assets needs an App Store Connect key with the App Manager role; Diceroll's has Developer) and 'Replace the key'; Google Play uses the CDN with the baseline in the build (Play Asset Delivery only when chosen, because it ties packs to builds); itch.io and the download page use the CDN; Steam says depots once Steam is connected, with Connect Steam, consistent with Home.

The card's foot says 'transports.packs: auto' in .pkey/distribution and that a named transport wins, and confirms Updates is on; with Updates off, the attention item 'N packs declared, Updates is off: devices get embedded baselines only' replaces that line.

Wide: 'How packs reach players' is the aside beside the callout and the table. Phone: the sidebar folds into the menu button, the callout's button drops under its text, each pack stacks behind its labels, and each channel's link drops under its text.

designReview.reviewer: 4 UX designers, triaged by a lead designer
designReview.verdict: Spacing and copy trimmed per the multi-review triage; see findings.

findings.issue: Lopsided wide layout; the rail is twice the table height and repeats the CDN label four times.
findings.resolution: 'How packs reach players' sits under the table as a two-column list below 1600px and is the sticky rail from there; one 'Polaris Key's CDN' row lists the channels, only exceptions get rows (App Store key, Play Asset Delivery opt-in, Steam not connected); intro and 'Updates is on' sentence deleted; footer 'Override with transports.packs in .pkey/distribution'.

findings.issue: Gate is a dash on three of four rows; the banner repeats the pill.
findings.resolution: Gate column dropped; Delivery shows 'Essential' or 'On demand' with its muted sub-line, the 'To approve' pill and gate name in the supporter row; banner 'diceroll.supporter.skins 1.4.0 needs one approval' with Approve on Access, full width and 44px on phone.

findings.issue: [Phone] Code blocks, terminals and tab strips are silently clipped with no scroll cue; 'also required' cuts Info.plist and Docker.
findings.resolution: Kit: .fade-x (edge fade, tabindex 0, role region) and .wrap-phone (soft wrap at 12px on phone) on every code block and terminal; 'also required' is a dot. Gutters (16 phone, 24 up) and card padding (16 phone, 24 up) were already the kit's.

findings.issue: [Wide] Single-column screens hug the left of a 1920 canvas; the rail leaves 600-750px empty.
findings.resolution: Kit: .page.contained (1280, centred), .page.form.centered, and .sticky-rail (360px rail, sticky at top 88px from 1600px); card pairs use .top (align-items:start).
